correctness.rationale: The full orthogonal spectral decomposition is elementary and exhaustive; group averaging makes the invariant optimum globally valid. For fixed spoke weight, clique weight can null its eigenspace and cycle-edge weight is uniquely balanced between the two extreme rim modes; the balancing point is feasible for all m>=4. A one-dimensional minimax has a unique crossing-or-hub-budget solution. The exact residual clique interval proves the global support transitions by nonnegative averaging; asymptotics follow from cosine endpoints. The current package path verify.py ran 3929 cross-checks, including exact rational calculations, direct full-matrix spectral comparisons, and independent linear programming on 370 graph sizes. Finite checks do not replace the family proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison separates the published one-hub wheel optimum and the general clique-lift reduction from the new exact all-parameter clique–cycle solution, entire invariant optimizer interval, two core-edge support boundaries, and two-branch size-ratio law. Dedicated research-record and literature searches did not find a statement implying those results, though an unindexed analytic specialization remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis or specialized nonuniform-wheel FMRMC derivation may state an equivalent closed-form answer.
The general clique-lifting theorem sharply reduces novelty scope; the claim must be understood as an explicit solved base-case family and new transition classification, not as a novel lift principle.

value.rationale: A complete infinite two-size family with an explicit optimal random walk and all invariant optimizers is a natural problem beyond the standard wheel. Sharp thresholds show when internal core edges are structurally forbidden, optional, or indispensable even without imposing symmetry, and limit to the nontrivial core-to-rim size ratios 1/2 and 1. These precise support-allocation and asymptotic facts motivate the computation and are not routine evaluation of one small graph.
